page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.4xlarge is a general purpose instance engineered around AWS custom silicon and the Nitro hypervisor framework. Powered by the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture, the system provides 16 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, avoiding resource contention typical of simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 64 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per core. Network connectivity delivers an 8 Gbps baseline throughput.

A distinguishing feature of this configuration is the bundled 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage, providing low-latency disk operations directly attached to the host. In benchmark evaluations, the architecture achieves top-tier results in single-threaded compression algorithms, including gzip compression at 36.48 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.31 GB/sec, alongside a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2393.0. The memory subsystem also benchmarks in the upper tier with a PassMark memory score of 4380.5, while PassMark database operations and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression demonstrate strong performance.

Relative to raw compute workloads, standard stress-ng benchmarks register in the median tier across single-core and multi-core evaluations, indicating that performance scales best on software compiled specifically for ARMv9 instruction sets. The absence of discrete GPUs limits its application for massive parallel model training, though medium-sized language model inference achieves competitive token generation throughput. With its combination of dedicated physical cores, balanced memory density, and bundled NVMe instance storage, m9gd.4xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for transactional databases, caching tiers like Redis, build environments, microservices, and static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.4xlarge is a general purpose instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz without multithreading, alongside 64 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. In addition to 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, the configuration includes 950 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, eliminating network latency overhead for temporary data sets. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compression performance and single-core Geekbench metrics, supplemented by strong multi-core throughput and robust memory subsystem scores. While stress-ng execution sits within middle tiers, high throughput in static web serving and database operations highlights its balanced architecture. The instance delivers high resource efficiency for ARM-optimized applications, making it well matched for transactional databases, caching layers, containerized microservices, data processing pipelines, and static web serving workloads requiring low-latency instance-store disk access.
